abstract:
Transcriptomic drug repurposing identifies candidate therapeutics by comparing disease-associated expression states with drug-induced perturbations. Most existing connectivity-based approaches use individual genes as the primary representation units, potentially overlooking the coordinated transcriptional programs that organize cellular states and disease phenotypes. Whether transcriptional programs can provide a biologically meaningful representation layer for therapeutic connectivity mapping remains largely unexplored.
We introduce ProReT, a context-dependent transcriptional program-space framework for interpretable transcriptomic drug repurposing. ProReT projects disease and drug signatures into biologically derived programs and quantifies reversal using regularized Gram whitening. Using K562 and KOLF2.1J program references, we analyzed 28 disease views and benchmarked 25 coverage-qualified views across 1,728 compounds. In the K562 example, program representations retained same-drug and same-mechanism-of-action organization and outperformed selected generic dimensionality-reduction baselines. Reference choice produced distinct disease representations and therapeutic rankings. In multiple myeloma, ProReT prioritized established proteasome inhibitors and linked reversal to proteostasis, translation, and stress programs, while an independent cohort reproduced the overall compound-ranking structure. Together, these results support transcriptional programs as an interpretable intermediate representation that complements gene-level connectivity in context-dependent therapeutic prioritization.
ProReT is available as an open-source R package at https://github.com/jiazhiren201988/ProReT, including versioned program references and example multiple myeloma datasets for reproducible analysis. Archived releases and reference resources are available at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21943239).
Supplementary material is available at Bioinformatics online.
